/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

{slug}

{children}
) } ``` If this param is dynamic (not provided by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)), it is runtime data and the layout cannot be prerendered.

{slug}

{children}
) } ``` If this param is dynamic (not provided by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)), it is runtime data and the layout cannot be prerendered.

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

The `cacheLife` function is used to set the cache lifetime of a function or component. It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component.

## Usage

### Basic setup

To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:

title: use cache
description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

> **Good to know:**
>

The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.

00003| description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
00004| related:

00011| 
00012| Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
00013| 
00014| ## Usage
00015| 
00016| To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching):
00017| 
00018| ```ts filename="next.config.ts"
00019| import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
00020| 
00021| const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
00022|   cacheComponents: true,
00023|   partialPrefetching: true,
00024| }
00025| 
00026| export default nextConfig
00027| ```
00028| 
00029| Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
00030| 
00031| > **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime and does not support the [`runtime` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime). Remove any `runtime` export, including `runtime = 'nodejs'` and the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`. Other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
00032| 
00033| When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
00034| 
00035| - The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
00036| - The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
00037| - The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
00038| 
00039| > **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). import Link from 'next/link'
import type { ReactNode } from 'react'
import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'

export default async function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <nav>
          <Link href="/">Signal Shop</Link>
        </nav>
        {children}
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
